Hi Julia —

Appreciate the metadata. Quick answers up front, then I'll loop in Dev for SCIM specifics: 

- Required SAML attributes: email (primary identifier), groups (optional but recommended), and a role attribute (we typically accept 'roles' or 'entitlements'). We also support nmTenant or orgId for multi-tenant mappings if you prefer an explicit claim.
- Group->role mapping: Redwood's Private Control Plane supports both server-side mapping (we map incoming groups to internal roles) and client-side pre-population. For most customers we recommend server-side mapping (simpler updates) unless you need deterministic provisioning before user login.
- Service accounts: we use short-lived signed JWTs for system-to-system authentication; for Private we integrate with your IdP to mint service tokens via an OAuth client_credentials flow or with a signed cert exchange. We can also support HSM-backed service keys if you need FIPS/HSM.

1) Dev to confirm SCIM group sync permissions and whether group-membership delta push is supported.
2) Laura to prepare a sample SAML attribute mapping document and a proposed role matrix for Acme.
3) Oliver to provide SCIM schema/export (Oliver noted this is coming).

I'll set a 30-min call for next week to walk through the mappings and a quick test plan. Does Weds 11/18 at 10AM PT work?

Thanks,

Thanks — adding technical detail on SCIM and the mapping behavior.

Summary (SCIM):
- We support SCIM 2.0 with PATCH/PUT and full user/group provisioning. For groups we support add/remove member deltas and full-sync.
- Permissions needed on your SCIM service account: read:Users, write:Users, read:Groups, write:Groups. If you provide an Okta API token with Group read/write scope we can run test syncs.
- Mapping options:
  * Server mapping (recommended): Redwood accepts group membership and uses an internal mapping table (group-name -> Redwood role). This allows central updates without modifying your IdP.
  * Attribute mapping (IdP side): some customers prefer IdP to set a 'roles' SAML claim; Redwood will accept and persist that claim at login. Note: role revocation timing depends on token TTLs.

SAML specifics:
- Recommended attributes: NameID (email), givenName, familyName, groups, roles/entitlements (string array).
- Suggested assertion lifetime: <= 5 minutes to avoid stale role grants. We also support assertion_in_response_to checks and audience restriction.
- For attribute mapping we can ingest an 'redwood_role' attribute that maps 1:1 to internal RBAC roles.

Service account & automation:
- For cluster automation we recommend: OAuth client_credentials with short-lived tokens (1h), rotated by your IdP. Alternatively, we support a signed CSR flow: you provide a service cert signed by your CA and Redwood rotates a short-lived internal token bound to the cert.
- We'll avoid long-lived static keys unless requested.

I'll attach a sample scim-group-mapping.xlsx and a draft saml-attribute-mapping-draft.md to this thread.

Julia —

Thanks for sending the metadata. I've drafted a mapping matrix attached (scim-group-mapping.xlsx) and a short SAML attribute mapping doc (saml-attribute-mapping-draft.md). High-level notes:

- We'll map Acme Okta groups to these Redwood roles by default: 
  * acme-admins -> redwood_admin
  * acme-platform-engineers -> redwood_deployer
  * acme-readonly -> redwood_viewer

- If you'd rather keep mapping inside Okta (roles claim), we can skip server mapping and instead accept the roles claim. We recommend server mapping for production (easier rollback).
- For SCIM sync we suggest running a dry-run with read-only access first, then enable write on the next window.
- Test plan for 11/18 call:
  1) Exchange IdP metadata and confirm SP ACS and Audience.
  2) Configure SCIM test account (read-only).
  3) Run a group delta and validate mapping on Redwood side.
  4) Promote service account to write for final sync and confirm members.
